note: Scenario-based manual evaluation prompts. These have not been run against a live Claude Code instance in this environment.

evals.prompt: I have a 14-page ML paper and only 12 minutes for a conference talk. The paper has four figures and six tables. Design the narrative and a slide storyboard without dumping every section. Distinguish what results prove from what we speculate.
evals.expected_behavior: Audience-driven central claim; motivation→insight→decisive evidence→limits; scoped methods; claim-evidence traceability; action titles; explanation and timing; no invented data.

evals.prompt: We need a 6-slide exec briefing about whether to delay launch. Ship date is May 15, two bugs remain, 20% of production traffic is affected in tests. Produce the decision arc and tell me what evidence is missing.
evals.expected_behavior: Answer-first/BLUF recommendation only if defensible; explicit unknown impact assumptions; options/risk/ask/owner; no motivational pitch or fake statistics.

evals.prompt: Teach approximate nearest neighbor search to developers who know databases but not vector search. First give a 7-minute spoken explanation with at most 6 slides; use a running example and explain recall/latency trade-off.
evals.expected_behavior: Audience prerequisites and one concrete example; intuition then mechanism; meaningful visuals; correct caveat about approximation; speaker phrasing distinct from slide text.

evals.prompt: My 18 slides all have dark-blue gradients, three rounded cards per page, and slogans like 'Unlock synergies'. Critique the design and rewrite one typical slide about reducing approval handoffs. Do not invent metrics.
evals.expected_behavior: Specific anti-template diagnosis; information-first redesign; grounded language and diagram; before/after example; no invented numerical performance.

evals.prompt: I have 37 bullet points listing what my team did this month. Make a 5-minute status presentation for engineering leadership. Prioritize blockers and decision needs; do not make it a generic victory lap.
evals.expected_behavior: State vs plan→change→impact→risks→ask structure; cuts appendix items; logic beats activity list; avoids invented issues.

evals.prompt: Prepare a graduate-level mini-seminar where the core object is a single dense theorem proof. I need the formal statement, assumptions and proof sketch, not TED-style storytelling. Suggest how to visually stage it.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not overcut precision or force artificial tension; manages prereqs and reveals; preserves formalism; scope/evidence correct.

evals.prompt: Turn a 30-page audit memo into a presentation for a meeting, but the same file will be sent to stakeholders who weren't there. Show how you would serve both audiences without 10-point slide text.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes dual-use issue; sparse live slides plus notes/appendix or separate leave-behind; preserving qualifications and provenance.

evals.prompt: Design a 20-minute hands-on training session explaining SQL window functions to analysts. Most attendees know GROUP BY. Include learning checks and one worked example, not a feature inventory.
evals.expected_behavior: Audience dependency ladder; tasks and worked examples; real learner participation and pacing; no list-dump.

evals.prompt: Here are correlations between user engagement and time-on-site. Build a stakeholder slide claiming our new feature caused the retention improvement.
evals.expected_behavior: Rejects causal overclaim; makes observational finding and its limitations clear; proposes causal tests/alternatives; truthful titles and chart design.
